meta.title: Sony Bravia · Commercial Command Center
meta.subtitle: A quarter of continuous collection, extrapolated from the measured snapshot
meta.subject: sony

disclosure.headline: The figures on these screens are extrapolated, not measured.
disclosure.body: Every Sonos lane we hold today is a single capture. This dashboard answers what a quarter of continuous collection would look like: the measured snapshot is used as an anchor and a 13-week daily panel is simulated around it, with retail-calendar seasonality, promotional cycles, stock episodes and competitive response. Levels are pinned to what was measured; shapes are modelled. Nothing here should be read as a reported result.

anchors.measured: Street price, list price, discount rate and offer count for 23 Amazon listings across 4 brands, monthly 2025-12 to 2026-05
anchors.pins: Every daily price ladder is bounded by its brand's measured discount rate — Sony Bravia 5.1%, Samsung 1.2%, LG 11.9%, TCL 19.7%.

anchors.measured: PDP shelf price for 9 models across 5 retailers, captured 2026-08-13
anchors.pins: Each simulated ladder is scaled to land on the captured price at the capture date.

anchors.measured: 68 promotion verbatims across 14 product pages, each located and outlined in the captured image
anchors.pins: The mechanic set, the per-retailer mix, and every promotion type shown.
Carried and not-carried cells are held fixed; only 'not readable' cells are extrapolated.

anchors.measured: Share of days in the last audited month with a buyable Amazon offer — Sony Bravia 100%, Samsung 100%, LG 72%, TCL 100%
anchors.pins: The target in-stock rate each simulated episode series is drawn against.

anchors.measured: 33 delivery-promise readings across 9 models, 5 retailers and 6 cities
anchors.pins: Week-one lead time for every model-retailer-city triple that was captured.

anchors.measured: Share of the result grid per retailer per search term across 3 terms, 3 passes
anchors.pins: The level each daily shelf-share series reverts to.

anchors.measured: Share of the AI answer across 3 engines by funnel stage. Any engine shown on the dashboard beyond those is modelled off their mean and is a column of illustration, not a measurement.
anchors.pins: The per-engine and per-stage level each daily series reverts to, for the engines that were captured.

anchors.measured: Amazon star rating weighted by rating count, and monthly aspect scores from captured reviews across 8 aspects
anchors.pins: Rating levels, and every aspect month that had a real reading is passed through untouched.

anchors.measured: Monthly visits, US share, bounce rate, pages per visit, visit duration, leading channel and country mix for 3 of 4 brand domains — sony.com 38.6M, lg.com 36.2M, tcl.com 6.1M. samsung.com captured but WITHHELD: the domain is not a fair proxy for the product line, so the whole lane is null for that brand rather than modelled. sony.com and lg.com are whole-domain reads: real, but covering more than this category, and labelled that way wherever they appear.
anchors.pins: The session level for each measured brand, its bounce, pages per visit and duration, its leading channel share, and its country mix. NOT the day-to-day shape — the profile publishes a monthly figure, so the movement across the quarter is still modelled — not the rest of the channel split, which sits behind a subscription, not add-to-cart, which is published nowhere, and not the retail product-page split, which is modelled from shelf presence and retailer weight.

disclosure.paletteNote: Sony’s own black fails the chroma and lightness checks for a categorical slot and reads as “no data”, and Samsung blue against LG red is the pair a reader most needs to be able to separate.

overview.text: Over the 13 weeks Sony Bravia holds 34.9% of the AI answer — first of the 4 — against 5.8% of the retail shelf, last of the 4. The brand is being recommended far more often than it is being seen on a result grid.
Price discipline is intact: Sony Bravia transacts at 90.9% of MSRP, first of the 4, while the set as a whole runs at 84%.
Share of category traffic sits at 55.4%, first of the 3, and moved +0.6pp between the open and the close of the quarter.
In-stock rate of 97.9% is first of the 4; 16 separate out-of-stock episodes cost 32 listing-days across the carried estate.

traffic.text: sony.com drew 38.60M visits worldwide last month, 37.3% of them from the United States — 14.39M US visits, measured rather than modelled. The day-to-day shape across the quarter is still modelled; the level is not. Read it as the brand's whole web presence: sony.com spans PlayStation, cameras and audio — Bravia is one line inside it.

Sony Bravia takes 55.4% of the tracked brand-site visits, first of the 3; LG is the nearest of the rest on 41.8%. Samsung is excluded: its own domain is not a fair proxy for the product line, so counting it would divide by a business this category is only a corner of. The comparison is domain against domain, not product line against product line — Sony Bravia and LG carry several categories on the same site.
Assistant referrals grew from 18.5k to 30.2k sessions a day across the quarter — a 63.5% rise, the fastest-growing channel in the mix.
Paid search carries 6% of Sony Bravia sessions, the least paid-dependent of the 3; TCL runs the most paid-dependent mix at 18.4%.

ai.text: Sony Bravia is first of the 4 on share of the AI answer at 34.9%.
Presence is uneven by engine: Gemini returns Sony Bravia in 36.3% of answers against 33.1% on ChatGPT — a 3.1-point spread on the same prompt set.
The strongest funnel position is decision at 48.3%, the weakest awareness at 21.2%.

shelf.text: Shelf share of 5.8% puts Sony Bravia last of the 4; Samsung is the nearest of the rest on 28.6%.
Presence concentrates where the intent is specific — "mini led tv" returns Sony Bravia in 8.1% of the grid, against 4.5% on the weakest term.
7.2% of Sony Bravia shelf presence is paid — the least paid-reliant of the 4. Samsung buys its way onto the grid at 40.6%, which is why Sony Bravia share moves against it in event weeks.
Target reads thinnest for Sony Bravia at 0% of the grid, against 13.1% at Amazon — a 13.1-point gap between the brand's best and worst shelf.

distribution.text: Sony Bravia occupies 16 of 35 possible model-by-retailer cells — 42.3% weighted for the days each listing was actually live, last of the 4.
4 listings changed state inside the quarter: 1 dropped, 1 appeared, 2 lapsed and returned.
Buy-box ownership averages 93.2% on the marketplaces, first of the 4 — every point lost is a sale credited to a reseller at a price the brand did not set.

availability.text: In-stock rate of 97.9% is first of the 4; 16 out-of-stock episodes cost 32 listing-days over the quarter.
None of the 16 episodes followed a deep discount, so these are replenishment gaps rather than promotions outrunning supply. The longest ran 5 days on BRAVIA 9 65" at Newegg, from 2026-07-07.

delivery.text: The Sony Bravia delivery promise averages 3.9 days — the fastest of the 4, against 4.2 days for Samsung, the fastest of the rest.
The promise is not national: Miami, FL waits 4.4 days against 3.5 in Chicago, IL — a 0.9-day spread on the same catalogue.

pricing.text: Sony Bravia realises 90.9% of MSRP across the quarter, first of the 4 — the category runs 84% and TCL clears at 71.2%.
BRAVIA 8 II 65" carries the widest cross-retailer spread at $292.25 on average and $673.52 at its widest — a shopper comparing two tabs sees two different brands.
8 listings traded below the 85% floor for 180 days in total, worst at 12.8% under.

promotions.text: Sony Bravia runs a price promotion on 17.3% of carried listing-days — the second-least promoted of the 4. TCL is on promotion 31.2% of the time.
When Sony Bravia does promote it goes 7.7% deep against a category mean of 12.9% — the second-shallowest of the 4 on discount depth.
54.8% of Sony Bravia price events open inside a retail-calendar window, spread across 5 retailers; 42 episodic events ran in the quarter at a mean 8.8 days each.
The mechanic doing most of the work is protection plan at 32.5% of Sony Bravia promotional days.

tco.text: Attach-weighted, the shelf price understates what a Sony Bravia buyer actually pays by 0.5% — the narrowest of the 4. TCL shows a 1.8% gap, 3.6x wider, so a shelf-price comparison against it is not a like-for-like read.
BRAVIA 7 II 65" at Best Buy carries the widest single gap: $2598.43 on the shelf against $2587.57 attach-weighted, of which $208.08 is funded by the brand rather than the retailer.

8 of 15 Sony Bravia listings carry three or more simultaneous mechanics. The more mechanics on a page, the less the shelf price says about the transaction — and the harder a competitor's headline price is to read straight.

voice.text: Sony Bravia rates 4.31★, third of the 4; LG leads on 4.5★.
Review velocity of 2.4k over the quarter is last of the 4 — a smaller base to defend the rating with.
